title: Floating floor installation (underlay, expansion gaps)
audience: Floor installers and tilers who lay floating floors and are paid for the higher-rate work
learningOutcomes: Prepare a substrate and underlay for a floating floor to the manufacturer's requirements.
Leave expansion gaps at walls, fixed objects and transitions.
Identify where licence positions for floating floors are not established in each state.

instruction.heading: What a floating floor is, and why the product decides the method
instruction.body: A floating floor is laid over a substrate and is held together at its joints rather than bonded or fixed to the substrate. Because it is not fixed down, the whole floor can move as one piece, and most of the installation rules come from that movement. Products differ. Laminate, engineered timber and vinyl plank are installed in different ways, and each manufacturer's instructions set the joint method, the order of laying, the tools and the underlay. Read those instructions before quoting or starting, and keep a copy in the job file. This lesson gives the principles that apply to most floating floors. It does not replace the product's own method.

instruction.heading: Substrate flatness and moisture
instruction.body: The substrate must be sound, clean and flat within the tolerance the manufacturer gives. Check flatness with a straight edge and a feeler gauge across the area, and mark any high or low spot for grinding, filling or levelling by the method the product allows. Moisture is the most common cause of floating floor failure, so measure it before any underlay goes down. Use the test method the manufacturer names, record the reading, and record the method used. Where the reading is over the limit, stop. A moisture barrier is installed only where the product calls for one, and only as the product directs. Do not lay a floating floor over a substrate that is wet, sweating or showing signs of rising damp. A surface that looks dry is not a measurement, and the reading decides.

instruction.heading: Underlay, acclimatisation and the sample row
instruction.body: Confirm the underlay type with the product before buying it, because some underlay forms part of the manufacturer's conditions. Acclimatise the planks or boards in the room, flat and unopened where the product allows, for the time the manufacturer gives, so that they reach the room's temperature and humidity before they are laid. Lay the underlay as directed, with seams taped or overlapped as specified and turned up at the walls where the product requires it. Start the first run against a straight reference line, check it for square, and lay a sample row before committing to the layout. Check the end-piece lengths the product allows, so that a short last piece does not appear against a wall. Mix boards from several cartons as you go, so that no shade band or pattern repeat shows across the room.

instruction.heading: Expansion gaps at walls, fixed objects and pipes
instruction.body: A floating floor moves with changes in temperature and humidity, so it needs an expansion gap at every wall, fixed object, pipe, column, cabinet base and threshold. The gap width comes from the manufacturer's data, and it is not a figure to estimate. Set the gap with spacers during laying, check it at every run, and remove the spacers at the end. Cover the gap with the approved trim, skirting or transition, and fix the trim to the wall or the skirting rather than to the floor, so that the floor can still move beneath it. A floor laid tight to a wall has nowhere to go when it expands, and it then buckles or lifts. Do not hide the gap with sealant unless the manufacturer allows it, because sealant can lock the floor in place and transfer the movement to the joints.

instruction.heading: Transitions, doorways and large areas
instruction.body: Each doorway, threshold and change of floor covering needs an approved transition strip or trim that allows the floor to move. Where the floor runs a long distance in one direction, the manufacturer may require an intermediate movement joint or a transition. A transition fixed rigidly across the joint can stop the movement and cause the same damage as a tight wall. Choose the transition to suit the height difference between the two floors and the direction of the joint, and fix it as the product directs. Record each transition, its type and its fixing, and photograph the joint before the trim covers it.

instruction.heading: Finishing, handover and the client's conditions
instruction.body: Remove all spacers before the room is used, and check each joint and each transition for lift, squeaks and a hollow sound. Clean the floor using only the products the instructions allow. Explain the conditions that affect the floor, such as keeping the room within the temperature and humidity range the manufacturer gives, using the mats and furniture protection the manufacturer recommends, and not dragging heavy furniture across it. Give the client the product information and the record of the moisture reading, underlay, gaps and transitions. A warranty is the manufacturer's to give, on the manufacturer's terms. Do not describe any warranty as given by the installer unless the written terms say so.

procedure: Read the manufacturer's installation instructions and confirm the underlay, the gap widths and the moisture limit before the job starts.
Check the substrate for flatness and sound condition, and mark any high or low spots for the method the product allows.
Measure the substrate moisture by the manufacturer's method, and record the reading and the method.
Install the moisture barrier and the underlay as the manufacturer directs, with seams taped or overlapped as specified.
Acclimatise the product for the manufacturer's time, then check the layout and the end-piece lengths.
Lay a sample row, check the square and the gaps, and then lay the floor with spacers at every wall and fixed object.
Fit the approved transitions and trims, fixed as directed, and remove the spacers.
Check for squeaks, lift and hollow sounds, and record the moisture reading, underlay product, gap widths and transitions.

workedExamples.situation: A floating floor in a sunroom was laid tight against the walls to hide the gap. In summer the owner reports that boards have lifted near the glass and that one row has pushed up against the skirting.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the most likely cause, what do you check, and what do you say to the owner?
workedExamples.reasoning: The most likely cause is that the floor could not expand, because the gap at the walls was missing or too small for the room's heat and humidity. Check the gap at each wall against the manufacturer's figure, check the transitions and any fixed objects, and look for the substrate moisture record if one exists. Record what is found, with photographs. Do not press the lifted boards down, because that loads the joints further. Refer the floor for re-laying to the manufacturer's gap requirement, and quote the work separately, including any trim or transition that has to be replaced. The lesson does not confirm whether the glazing or the sun exposure contributed; the manufacturer's advice governs the answer.

workedExamples.situation: (Example job) A laundry slab has a damp patch after a cold morning. The client asks for a floating floor to be laid this week to match the bedroom.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you lay the floor this week?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Measure the substrate moisture by the manufacturer's method and record the reading. If it is over the limit, the floor cannot be laid until the cause is found and the substrate is within the limit, or a barrier is used as the product allows. A damp patch can come from a water source rather than from the slab, and finding that source is outside floor installation, so refer it to a competent person. Tell the client that the programme depends on the reading, and do not lay the floor to meet the date.

workedExamples.situation: (Example job) A new floating floor meets an existing tiled entry at a doorway. The threshold has a height difference, and the client asks for the floor to run through without a strip.
workedExamples.reasoning: Not without checking the product. Choose an approved transition that suits the height difference and the joint direction, and show the client the option and why it is needed. Fit it so that it allows movement, and record the transition type and its fixing. Where the manufacturer does not approve a continuous run at that joint, a transition is required, and the client's preference does not override the product's requirement.

equipmentAndPpe: Manufacturer's installation instructions, with the approved underlay and any barrier named in them
Spacers set to the manufacturer's gap width
Moisture meter, or the test kit the manufacturer names, with a record sheet
Straight edge, feeler gauge and spirit level
Tape measure, square, pencil and chalk line
Underlay cutter, utility knife and seam tape
Tapping block and pull bar, as the product requires
Eye protection, gloves and knee pads; hearing protection and a dust mask where a power saw is used, with cutting controls as set out in “Cutting tile and silica dust controls”

commonErrors.error: Laying a floating floor tight to the walls or to fixed objects.
commonErrors.prevention: Leave the manufacturer's gap at every wall, pipe, column and fixed object, and check it on every run.

commonErrors.error: Laying a floating floor over a damp or unchecked substrate.
commonErrors.prevention: Measure the moisture by the manufacturer's method, record the reading, and do not start over the limit.

commonErrors.error: Skipping acclimatisation and laying boards straight from the carton.
commonErrors.prevention: Acclimatise the product for the manufacturer's time in the room where it will be laid.

commonErrors.error: Filling the expansion gap with sealant, or fixing the trim to the floor.
commonErrors.prevention: Fix trims to the wall or skirting, and use sealant only where the manufacturer allows it.

commonErrors.error: Omitting or misplacing the transition at a doorway.
commonErrors.prevention: Choose and fit the approved transition at each doorway and change of floor covering, and record it.

commonErrors.error: Leaving spacers in place, or leaving a short end piece against a wall.
commonErrors.prevention: Remove the spacers at the end, and check the end-piece lengths in the sample row before laying.

commonErrors.error: Describing a warranty that the installer cannot give.
commonErrors.prevention: Give the manufacturer's warranty information, and record the product, underlay and gap widths.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: New South Wales: the NSW Government tiling page covers wall and floor tiling work valued at more than $5,000 in labour and materials, including GST. It refers to cork, linoleum, rubber and thermoplastic tiles, but it does not name floating floors. Confirm it with Building Commission NSW before accepting work.
Queensland: the QBCC wall and floor tiling class names ceramic, glass, marble, slate, stone and terracotta, and it does not name floating floors, vinyl or laminate.

Victoria: Consumer Victoria's registration page says that a job involving only one listed trade, including installing floor coverings or tiling (wall and floor), does not need registration, and that combining skills on one job does.

South Australia: the CBS guide says anyone carrying on business as a building work contractor must hold the right licence. It sets no dollar threshold for licensing and does not name tiling, floor coverings or floating floors.

This lesson does not grant a licence for floating floors in any state or territory. Floating floors are not named on the NSW or QBCC tiling pages; the licence position is not confirmed by an official source.
Completing this lesson does not give a floor covering, tiling or building licence. Confirm the licence position with the state regulator before accepting work in any state or territory.

Underlay tapes, primers and any adhesive used with the product may be hazardous chemicals. Each product should have a current SDS. A compliant SDS has 16 headings, and a copy is available from the supplier at no cost on request.

Cartons of flooring and rolls of underlay are heavy and awkward to move. Safe Work Australia's model Code of Practice on hazardous manual tasks says that manual tasks must be identified and their risks assessed and managed.
No national standard for floating floor installation was identified in the research.

qualityStandard: The substrate is flat within the manufacturer's tolerance, and the moisture reading is within the limit and recorded before the underlay is laid.
Every wall, fixed object, pipe and threshold has the manufacturer's expansion gap, checked on every run.
Transitions are fitted at every doorway and change of floor covering, as approved for the product, and they allow movement.
The floor is free of squeaks, lift and hollow sounds after the spacers are removed.
The licence position for floating floors in the state is confirmed with the regulator before the work is accepted.
documentationEvidence: Substrate and moisture record, with the method, the reading and the limit
Underlay and barrier product record, with the manufacturer's instruction reference
Gap and transition record, with photographs taken before the trims cover the joints
Written confirmation of the licence position for floating floors in the state
summary: Confirm the manufacturer's method, underlay and moisture limit before starting.
Check flatness and moisture, and record the reading before any underlay goes down.
Leave the manufacturer's gap at every wall and fixed object, and do not seal or fix the gap tight.
Fit approved transitions, and confirm the licence position for the state before accepting work.

knowledgeChecks.question: A floating floor is laid tight against the walls. Why is this a problem?
options: It improves the look of the floor and its finish
It removes the need for underlay beneath the boards
The floor cannot expand, so it may buckle or lift
It has no effect on the floor at any point

knowledgeChecks.question: The substrate moisture reading is above the manufacturer's limit. What is correct?
options: Lay the floor anyway, since the reading is only slightly high, and check the floor after a month of normal use in the house
Stop, and do not lay the floor until the cause is dealt with and the reading is within the limit, or the product's remedy is used
Press the floor down hard with a roller to seal the moisture in the boards, the subfloor and the joists below
Lay the floor over a thicker underlay only, since it will block the moisture from rising up into the floor boards above

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the purpose of a transition strip at a doorway?
options: To cover the joint between two floors while allowing the floor to move
To fix the floor rigidly to the slab beneath it at every point
To hide the expansion gap with a bead of sealant along the edge
To replace the need for an underlay under the floor boards at the door
